causal_history.claim: Standalone lifecycle events were claimed to flow through one message-owned timeline.

causal_history.result: 6 of 16 fresh valid perturbations passed; the claimed unified lifecycle model was disproved.

causal_history.status: model replacement specified; production implementation not yet accepted

invariant: Sequence lifecycle layout is a normalized event model, not a collection of independent depth scans. The owner domain contains AbstractMessage, GroupingLeaf at GroupEnd, and no owner. Attachment ownership is distinct from whether a lifecycle type is accepted into an AbstractMessage's ordered type history: an unrelated lifecycle event after a self-message remains attached for ordinate placement but is excluded from combined-row classification. A message reserves the Java combined row only when its first accepted lifecycle type is ACTIVATE and a later accepted type is DEACTIVATE or DESTROY. Those message start/end ordinates install variations on one participant live-segment timeline. Message arrows, external arrows, notes, activation bars, group ranges, and final horizontal extents query that timeline. ComponentRoseArrow cross geometry is transformed from the complete spatial arrow area built from left and right live segments, not from a separately shifted semantic-source coordinate. Actual element extents produce one final envelope consumed by all external directions and GraphicalDivider. Earlier valid ordered ArrowConfiguration, autonumber, and chrome-stacking invariants remain in force.
causal_divergence: Implementation d01dd24e does not implement the claimed normalized model. Its last_message_owner ignores GroupEnd and therefore retains a prior message where Java replaces lastEventWithDeactivate with GroupingLeaf. Its owner_has_activation boolean loses accepted lifecycle-type order, so a later activation can retroactively make a deactivation-first owner look activation-first. It also conflates lifecycle attachment with row-classification eligibility, allowing unrelated participant events to classify a self-message even though AbstractMessage#addLifeEvent filters their types. Source-cross placement is derived from direction-specific from_x_shifted formulas, while Java first constructs a spatial MessageArrow area from both live segments and paints each dressing in component-local coordinates. Finally, note placement, lost-message extents, activation bars, group extents, painted endpoints, and divider width each replay activation or extent state independently. Java applies lifecycle variations once to LifeLine, registers actual graphical elements with group structures, resolves actual widths in prepareMissingSpace, and passes one final width to every drawable. The observed false combined rows, active-source cross displacement, note shifts, oversized group range, stale divider span, and wrong right-border depth are consequences of those ownership and data-flow differences, not coordinates to tune.
planned_change: Replace the competing event replays with one typed sequence layout model. First normalize each lifecycle command to an owner in {AbstractMessage, GroupingLeaf, None}, preserving GroupStart ownership and replacing it at GroupEnd. Record attachment separately from AbstractMessage type acceptance, including the self-message participant filter, and retain accepted lifecycle types in order. Derive each message's combined-row predicate and start/end ordinates from that record. Apply all lifecycle variations once to a queryable participant live-segment timeline. Build ordinary and external arrow areas from the left and right live segments at the message ordinate, then transform ArrowConfiguration dressings, including source crosses, through the component-local area. Derive note segments over their top and bottom ordinates, activation bars, and group membership from the same timeline and actual element geometry. Resolve one final horizontal constraint envelope from actual elements and use it for group frames, notes, all four external directions, and dividers. Remove or reduce note active_depth, lost_scan_activation, ActivationTracker/open_activations, group_act_depth, render_activation, and ad hoc live-depth helpers to views over the normalized model. Preserve the earlier ordered arrow grammar, DecimalFormat/autonumber behavior, and fractional chrome stack. Do not add branches keyed to fixture names, labels, participant counts, source coordinates, rendered coordinates, or observed 5-pixel, 6-pixel, and 30-pixel differences.

invariants.invariant: The current lifecycle owner is an AbstractMessage, the GroupingLeaf created by GroupEnd, or no owner. Messages replace the owner, ordinary intervening events and GroupStart preserve it, and GroupEnd replaces it with GroupingLeaf. Only AbstractMessage owners can reserve a combined lifecycle row.
invariants.causal_divergence: Rust tracks only last_message_owner and does not handle Event::GroupEnd, so lifecycle commands after a group end remain attached to the message that preceded the boundary.
invariants.planned_change: Normalize lifecycle attachment with an explicit owner enum and Java's replacement rules before deriving any row or depth state.

invariants.invariant: A combined row exists only when the first accepted lifecycle type is ACTIVATE and a later accepted type is DEACTIVATE or DESTROY.
invariants.causal_divergence: owner_has_activation is an unordered boolean. A later activation can make a deactivation-first sequence reserve a row that Java does not reserve.
invariants.planned_change: Retain accepted lifecycle types in order, or an equivalent state machine that records first_accepted_is_activate and later closing-type presence.

invariants.invariant: An unrelated participant's lifecycle event after a self-message remains attached to that message for ordinate placement, but AbstractMessage excludes its type from combined-row classification.
invariants.causal_divergence: Rust uses one owner relation for both ordinate attachment and type classification, so unrelated events can create a false self-message combined row.
invariants.planned_change: Store attachment owner and accepted-for-owner-classification as separate fields on every normalized lifecycle entry.

invariants.invariant: The complete spatial arrow area is bounded by the left and right live segments at the message ordinate. ArrowConfiguration selects component-local dressings, and source-cross geometry is transformed through that area.
invariants.causal_divergence: Rust derives the cross center from direction-specific from_x_shifted semantic-source formulas. That agrees only when the live segment collapses to an inactive point.
invariants.planned_change: Compute one spatial arrow area from both live segments and paint each dressing in component-local coordinates without an active-source correction constant.

invariants.invariant: Lifecycle variations are applied once to a participant timeline. Every message, note, activation bar, group member, and external arrow queries the same live segment at its relevant ordinate.
invariants.causal_divergence: Rust independently replays active_depth, lost_scan_activation, ActivationTracker/open_activations, group_act_depth, and render_activation, so consumers disagree after owner-preserving and owner-resetting events.
invariants.planned_change: Build one queryable live-segment timeline from normalized lifecycle entries and migrate every depth consumer to it before deleting the competing replays.
